Evaluate the gradient of the curve and normal at $A\left(1, \, \frac{1}{2}\right)$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=1} = -\frac{2}{(4(1) - 3)^2} = -2 \implies m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{-2} = \frac{1}{2}$$

Form and simplify the equation of the normal:
$$y - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}(x - 1) \implies y - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{1}{2} \implies y = \frac{1}{2}x$$

Equate the curve and the normal line $y = \frac{1}{2}x$:
$$\frac{1}{2(4x - 3)} = \frac{x}{2} \implies 1 = x(4x - 3) \implies 4x^2 - 3x - 1 = 0$$

Factorise and solve for the non-trivial intersection:
$$(4x + 1)(x - 1) = 0 \implies x = -\frac{1}{4} \quad (\text{or } x = 1)$$
$$\text{Required } x\text{-coordinate: } x = -\frac{1}{4}$$

Identify the given rate $\frac{dx}{dt} = -0.3\text{ units/s}$ (decreasing) and gradient $\frac{dy}{dx} = -2$ at $A$:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx} \times \frac{dx}{dt}$$

Calculate the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate:
$$\frac{dy}{dt} = -2 \times (-0.3) = 0.6 \text{ units per second}$$
